Title: Drive Awareness with Video Sequence Ads

URL Source: https://www.practicalecommerce.com/drive-awareness-with-video-sequence-ads

Published Time: 2026-09-09T15:22:09+00:00

Markdown Content:
Google Ads video sequence campaigns show multiple clips in a specific order to individual viewers. Sequence campaigns typically produce strong awareness and reach metrics, though other YouTube types are better known.

Other types likewise use multiple videos, but only sequence campaigns run in a predetermined progression. Google allows six sequence-campaign templates, each with a unique purpose:

*   **Introduce and reinforce.** Expose viewers to a brand through a long video, then reinforce it with a short one.
*   **Prompt and inspire.** Show viewers a short video, then inspire with a long one.
*   **Attract and direct.** Show viewers a short video, reinforce with a long video, then spur action with another short.
*   **Engage and differentiate.** Tell a brand story through four short videos.
*   **Custom sequence.** Advertisers choose the video combination and order.
*   **Automatic sequence.** Advertisers upload videos; Google optimizes the order.

### Campaign setup

To build a video ad sequence campaign, begin with “Create a campaign without guidance.” Then select the “Video” campaign type. Selecting the “YouTube reach, views, and engagements” option won’t show the ad sequence option.

[![Image 1: Screenshot of the Google Ads admin showing the options to choose](https://www.practicalecommerce.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/Video-Ad-sequence-objectives-570x262.jpg)](https://www.practicalecommerce.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/Video-Ad-sequence-objectives.jpg)

Select “Create a campaign without guidance” to start building a video ad sequence campaign.

Then choose the “Ad sequence” subtype and enter the campaign settings:

*   Daily or total budget
*   Start and end dates
*   Conversion goals
*   Geotargeting
*   [Audience segments](https://www.practicalecommerce.com/better-audience-targeting-in-google-ads)
*   Device targeting
*   Related videos to show below the ad

Video sequence advertisers can use only “target CPM” bidding and must set frequency capping to limit how often one person can see the sequence. The options are once every 7 or 30 days.

### Sequence setup

Each sequence step is an ad group. Four sequence steps equate to four ad groups. Each ad group contains:

*   The [YouTube video](https://www.practicalecommerce.com/understanding-youtube-campaign-types)
*   The ad formats (“skippable,” “bumper,” or “non-skippable”)
*   A call-to-action of 10 characters max
*   A headline of 15 characters max
*   A companion banner on desktop computers (to provide more exposure on larger screens).

Videos two and greater require step transitions in three choices: “impression,” “view,” or “skip.” For example, step two shows if the first video had an impression. Step three shows if the second video had a view. Advertisers can customize step transitions to create their desired narratives.

Google’s [Asset Studio](https://www.practicalecommerce.com/ai-creative-tools-in-google-ads) can shorten videos as needed via the”Trim videos” option. The tool works with various video formats and durations. Asset Studio can also create AI videos, though I avoid using them successively, if at all.

[![Image 2: Video frame in "Trim videos" option of a female](https://www.practicalecommerce.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/Trim-videos.jpg)](https://www.practicalecommerce.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/Trim-videos.jpg)

Google Asset Studio’s “Trim videos” option can shorten videos.

### Example

Say the marketers at Yarbo, maker of robot lawn mowers, want an “Introduce and reinforce” sequence. The team starts with the company’s demo video and trims it into two parts.

*   Introduce: 30-second video showcasing how the product works and its benefits.
*   Reinforce: 15-second video showing families enjoying the extra time from no yard work.

The first video’s headline is “Save Time. The CTA is “Learn more,” which links to the home page. Viewers now know the product and go to the main site to explore more.

The second video’s headline is “Labor Day Sale.” The CTA is “Buy now,” which links to the main product page.

The Yarbo team can test headlines and landing pages to reach the most potential customers.

Using this same demo video, the sequence could be four 15-second “Engage and differentiate” clips:

*   Step 1: What is Yarbo?
*   Step 2: Key features (wide blade width)
*   Step 3: Key benefits (more family time)
*   Step 4: Customer testimonials

### Interpreting results

Video ad sequence campaigns aim to generate demand and engagement. Google provides metrics such as:

*   Earned views: The number of ad viewers who then watched another video on the advertiser’s YouTube channel.
*   Video played: The percentage of viewers who watched 25%, 50%, 75%, or 100% of a video.
*   Unique users: The total number of viewers to the ad.

Advertisers can also track [clicks](https://www.practicalecommerce.com/ad-fraud-expert-on-scams-bots-spoofs) and conversions. But the goal, again, is engagement, which the three metrics above address. For example, a video needs work if only 10% of viewers watch 100% of it.

[![Image 1](https://substackcdn.com/image/fetch/$s_!I-pj!,w_1456,c_limit,f_auto,q_auto:good,fl_progressive:steep/https%3A%2F%2Fsubstack-post-media.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fpublic%2Fimages%2Fb0b973a1-8225-4828-b051-8074177f2178_1536x1024.png)](https://substackcdn.com/image/fetch/$s_!I-pj!,f_auto,q_auto:good,fl_progressive:steep/https%3A%2F%2Fsubstack-post-media.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fpublic%2Fimages%2Fb0b973a1-8225-4828-b051-8074177f2178_1536x1024.png)

**[ChatGPT Sites](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/sites?surface=app)** is one of the best new tools I've tried for making simple websites. I once spent hours drafting HTML by hand. I struggled with complex site-building software called Dreamweaver. Now making a good-looking site is as easy as creating a Google Doc.

Describe what you’re envisioning in a few sentences. Upload images or screenshots if you have a design in mind. Explain any special functionality you want, like linked buttons, embedded visuals, or interactive elements. ChatGPT Sites is in **[public beta](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/sites?surface=app)** and available for ChatGPT Plus, Pro, Business, Enterprise, and Edu plans.

To experiment this week, I made a **[companion guide](https://wonder-tools-chatgpt-sites.silverboat.chatgpt.site/)** for this post with ChatGPT Sites. Try it. I also created a new **[feedback page](https://wonder-tools-feedback.silverboat.chatgpt.site/)**. Add your private input about this or any other Wonder Tools post. [Share](https://wondertools.substack.com/p/chatgpt-sites?utm_source=substack&utm_medium=email&utm_content=share&action=share)

Given that I have no coding skills, I’ve been surprised that each site I’ve envisioned with ChatGPT has turned out better than I expected. Some **examples**:

(It’s a live online discussion group for paid subscribers.) Based on a background doc and context I shared, ChatGPT found and added cover thumbnails accurately. I prefer this site to the [prior version](https://jeremycaplan.github.io/wonder-tools-book-group/) I created with Claude Artifacts.

[![Image 2](https://substackcdn.com/image/fetch/$s_!kygn!,w_1456,c_limit,f_auto,q_auto:good,fl_progressive:steep/https%3A%2F%2Fsubstack-post-media.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fpublic%2Fimages%2F0e42d019-ac90-4318-accb-48ef47c50b13_1920x1080.png)](https://substackcdn.com/image/fetch/$s_!kygn!,f_auto,q_auto:good,fl_progressive:steep/https%3A%2F%2Fsubstack-post-media.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fpublic%2Fimages%2F0e42d019-ac90-4318-accb-48ef47c50b13_1920x1080.png) 

*   **[A guide](https://sf-weekend-event-guide.openai.chatgpt.site/)**to events in San Francisco**.**This looks much nicer than a typical Google Doc listing stuff to do during a visit.

*   **[A storefront](https://store-fronts-56.openai.chatgpt.site/field-day/)**for picnic supplies. A modern online store that lets you drag items into a basket. See the [prompt and iterations](https://developers.openai.com/showcase/field-day).

*   A **[marketing campaign](https://share-chatgpt-work.openai.chatgpt.site/)** page for ChatGPT Work with embedded social posts.

*   **[An announcement](https://chatgpt-sites-europe-launch.openai.chatgpt.site/)** that ChatGPT Sites is available in Europe.

*   **[An art making tool](https://goalflow.druekataoka.chatgpt.site/)**called GoalFlow. Choose a country’s flag and “paint” a new version with its colors on a fluid-simulation canvas. The paint swirls and drifts like pigment in water. Made by artist [Drue Kataoka](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/druekataoka_worldcup-goalflow-goalflow-activity-7483901380529741825--MEm/).

*   **[A music collection](https://now-thats-what-i-call-slop.openai.chatgpt.site/)** with embedded tracks. This one celebrates [Andrew Ambrosino](https://ambrosino.io/)’s batch of tracks about slop.

*   **[Glass Towers](https://glass-towers.openai.chatgpt.site/)**. A jenga-like game with realistic physics. See the [prompt and iterations](https://developers.openai.com/showcase/glass-towers) used to build it.

*   **[Paper Glider](https://paper-glider-56.openai.chatgpt.site/)**. A simple arcade game where you guide a paper airplane through hoops. See the [prompt and iterations](https://developers.openai.com/showcase/paper-glider).

*   **[Arcade Archive](https://arcade-archive-zh.xuxizhen.chatgpt.site/).**A playable collection of 8 classic video games.

1.   **Get started.**Select the **Sites** mode in ChatGPT. ([Screenshot](https://cln.sh/V7vLnhrv))

2.   **Specify your goal**. Describe a landing page, dashboard, guide, or app you want to build. **Tip:**mention who it’s for. That will help shape the interface.

3.   **Add context.**If you’re working within a ChatGPT Project, it will already have relevant context. It may have your style guide, logos, mission statement, and other files. If not, consider uploading whatever is relevant.

4.   **Provide visual guidance.**Note preferences you have for style, colors, fonts, or imagery. Consider adding reference images or screenshots of sites whose design you like. **Tip:**Tell ChatGPT to ask you questions before finalizing its approach. That helps you steer the plan.

5.   **Draw something if you want.**If you have a mockup in mind you can draw on paper, snap a photo of it and upload it as part of your query.

6.   **Give feedback.**As soon as ChatGPT gives you its first draft, reply with comments about what you’d like to change. Use the annotate tool in the sidebar to mark specific parts of the site to fix. Note where you want a color or font to be changed, a different image, or revised text.

7.   **Publish and share.**When your site is ready, publish the link to share it with others. Or keep it private if it’s a personal resource.

*   **Make a new landing page or portfolio.**If you don’t have a page showcasing your work, build one so people so people can learn more.

*   **Make a community resource.**Create a guide or topic overview based on your own insight or research. Share resources with students, friends, or the public.

*   **Make a useful app for yourself**. Address your own need. I made a private app to map out what I’m working on, pegged to publishing dates.

*   **Make a game.**Create something to make learning fun, or remake an old arcade/trivia title you loved. Customize its design and features so it’s distinct.

*   It’s not yet available on free ChatGPT plans.

*   If you use ChatGPT Sites heavily, you might hit a beta limit at some point. That will temporarily prevent you from creating new Sites or keeping high-usage Sites publicly available. I haven’t encountered that limit yet.

*   Sites don’t appear instantaneously. Depending on the complexity of what you’re building, expect to wait 10 or 15 minutes after submitting a prompt for your site to be ready.

*   [Help resources](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/sites?surface=app) are limited. For more guidance, the OpenAI Academy has a few [skills workshop recordings](https://academy.openai.com/home/search?query=sites&type=all). Or watch this helpful [video](https://youtu.be/1uAetuID7u0?si=vT_fPKkZxHoWUCbZ) by Paul Lipsky.

*   I used**[Tilda](http://tilda.cc/)** years ago to make my own [personal site](http://jeremycaplan.com/). It has excellent templates and gives you more manual control than any AI-first tool. It’s modular: swap in and adapt sections of your site without building from scratch. I [wrote](https://wondertools.substack.com/p/the-webs-best-kept-secret) about it in the early days of this newsletter.

*   **[Lovable](https://lovable.dev/invite/OTC6L9S)** and **[Bolt](https://bolt.cello.so/SrOsV4Xj47e)** are AI-first tools designed specifically for building sites. They’ve gotten easier to use and more flexible since I first [wrote](https://wondertools.substack.com/p/ai-for-coding?utm_source=publication-search) about vibe coding sites in 2024. If you’re already paying for ChatGPT, you may not need these other subscriptions since you can now build with ChatGPT Sites.

*   **[Claude](http://claude.ai/)** can make professional, interactive sites with [Artifacts](https://support.claude.com/en/articles/9487310-what-are-artifacts-and-how-do-i-use-them) and [Claude Design](https://claude.ai/design). It’s a superb choice if you’ve already provided Claude with deep context about your work and if you have a paid account. I’ve made lots of simple sites with Claude, and continue to use it alongside ChatGPT Sites.

kept.heading: DON'T MAKE THE MISTAKE OF BUYING ATTRIBUTION TOO SOON (5 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Custom attribution is premature until a channel has proven it works and the marketing mix is genuinely difficult to measure. Attribution helps answer where to put the next dollar across multiple working channels, not which channel works in the first place. Test channels first, then fix tracking, standardize ROAS, and model conversion value before building an attribution model. Custom attribution can pay off above roughly $3M in annual paid media, but the right threshold depends more on the complexity of the channel mix than the budget itself.
kept.article_text:
Title: Don’t make the mistake of buying attribution too soon

URL Source: https://www.021newsletter.com/p/dont-make-the-mistake-of-buying-attribution

Published Time: 2026-09-03T08:37:39+00:00

Markdown Content:
A lot of my sales calls (maybe too many, even) end with me telling someone not to buy anything from me.

They’ve come to me a year or two early, and I’d rather say so than take a deposit. The rule I use: can I convince myself they’ll make my fee back from the budget / channel mix changes the work leads to? A custom attribution build takes months and costs real money. If I can’t see impactful decisions waiting on the other side, there’s nothing for it to pay for.

I assumed that was uncontroversial.

Then we ran a [Propel](https://partnerwithpropel.com/) webinar on attribution in the warehouse, about as technical as our content gets. I went through the registrations afterwards. Half the people who joined were spending under $1M a year on ads.

In this article I cover the two questions worth asking before you sign off on an attribution project, why the spend threshold everyone quotes (including me) is a poor proxy for both, and what to build instead if the answers come back no.

Maybe this is an article you receive in my regular newsletter. Maybe this is an article that you directly received from me after booking a call for Propel and getting the “not now”.

The word covers almost anything now, so let me narrow it.

A custom model. It pulls your web and product analytics, your CRM, your ad platforms and usually the “how did you hear about us” answer into one place, then stitches them into a single view of the journey. One picture of how campaigns stack on each other, instead of four platforms all claiming the same conversion.

That’s heavy work. Here’s what it isn’t:

[![Image 1](https://substackcdn.com/image/fetch/$s_!YQd4!,w_1456,c_limit,f_auto,q_auto:good,fl_progressive:steep/https%3A%2F%2Fsubstack-post-media.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fpublic%2Fimages%2Fe9c533b6-5b9a-4134-8065-3339d07f091a_960x479.png)](https://substackcdn.com/image/fetch/$s_!YQd4!,f_auto,q_auto:good,fl_progressive:steep/https%3A%2F%2Fsubstack-post-media.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fpublic%2Fimages%2Fe9c533b6-5b9a-4134-8065-3339d07f091a_960x479.png)

Attribution is a lot, but it’s not these things

Most people who come to me want to find out what’s working. That’s an incrementality question, and a model is an expensive way to answer it. Turn the channel off in a few geos. Hold out part of the audience. See what happens. (I understand this is not as simple–but my recommendation for understanding _if_ something is working it’s usually to turn it off.)

Attribution answers something else. Several things are working, so where does the next chunk of budget go? That’s where it earns its money: catching channels eating each other, or branded search harvesting demand your YouTube spend created. I’ve written about a version of this split in[when to use click attribution or MMM](https://www.021newsletter.com/p/when-to-use-click-attribution-or-mmm).

Which means you need at least one channel already working. Otherwise there’s nothing to allocate between.

And when you’re small, that’s not hard to establish. You switch a channel on and the line goes up. Or it doesn’t. Two channels, low volumes, not much else it could have been.

The pattern I actually run into is different. Advertisers get to five or six channels before any of them has proved anything, then go looking for measurement to sort it out. That’s not a measurement problem. It’s a strategy problem wearing a measurement costume: too many channels, too early, none funded long enough to show a signal. A model will tell you that you have six channels and no evidence about any of them. Which is where you came in.

I stay out of growth advice here, so take this as an observation. When I see this, the advertiser is usually better off putting more money behind what already works than adding a seventh thing. (Nine times out of ten. Purely anecdotal, no study behind it, and I’d rather say so than dress it up as research.)

[![Image 2](https://substackcdn.com/image/fetch/$s_!Gpde!,w_1456,c_limit,f_auto,q_auto:good,fl_progressive:steep/https%3A%2F%2Fsubstack-post-media.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fpublic%2Fimages%2F77e101fb-5c75-4352-9c63-ffd6a7f9633b_1200x547.png)](https://substackcdn.com/image/fetch/$s_!Gpde!,f_auto,q_auto:good,fl_progressive:steep/https%3A%2F%2Fsubstack-post-media.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fpublic%2Fimages%2F77e101fb-5c75-4352-9c63-ffd6a7f9633b_1200x547.png)

With one channel you can see it working. With six you can’t, and a model won’t rescue you.

Say something is working. That’s not enough on its own, because plenty of setups are easy to measure with tools you already have.

This is where the spend threshold comes in, and where I have to own an oversimplification. Even Propel qualifies leads at $1M a year and up. It’s in our decks and on our site. It’s a proxy, and a rough one.

It works for a reason that has nothing to do with the number. Most brands spend their first million on Google, and Google is about as easy as attribution gets: high intent, a clear click path, a conversion in the same session. You don’t need a model for that. You need clean conversion tracking and someone reading the account properly. What changes higher up isn’t the spend. It’s what the money is buying.

[![Image 3](https://substackcdn.com/image/fetch/$s_!jHRw!,w_1456,c_limit,f_auto,q_auto:good,fl_progressive:steep/https%3A%2F%2Fsubstack-post-media.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fpublic%2Fimages%2F50535ec5-b9f4-4a94-bc5b-eb519aac9a47_832x791.png)](https://substackcdn.com/image/fetch/$s_!jHRw!,f_auto,q_auto:good,fl_progressive:steep/https%3A%2F%2Fsubstack-post-media.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fpublic%2Fimages%2F50535ec5-b9f4-4a94-bc5b-eb519aac9a47_832x791.png)

Some marketing / products are just damn difficult to measure

That last one is easy to miss. I worked on a wealth product where nearly everyone was in London. We ran out of Google before we ran out of budget, which forced a varied mix far earlier than the spend level suggested. The constraint was audience size, not ambition.

You think you would finish this article without having homework for your data team?

There’s still plenty to get on with, and it’s worth starting the moment one channel works.

**Get ROAS right.** Sounds solved, often isn’t. What counts as revenue, over what window, net of what costs, credited to which touchpoint. There’s a worked example in[the VEED ROAS report](https://www.021newsletter.com/p/veed-roas-marketing-report-paid-search-ads). **The check:** have two people calculate ROAS for the same campaign and month separately. If the numbers differ, that’s your project.

**Predict conversion value.** Ecommerce can skip this: you know the order value at conversion and pass it through (but obviously, it always depends: maybe you have many recurring purchases). For everyone else a signup is worth wildly different amounts, and if you hand the platforms one undifferentiated conversion they’ll find you more of the cheap ones. Modelling a predicted value and feeding it back makes a real difference on Google and Meta, where the algorithm does your allocation. **The check:** look at the spread of first-year revenue across last year’s conversions. If the top decile is worth several times the median, the platforms are optimising blind.

**Fix the tracking you have. Focus on data collection.** Least glamorous, often the highest return. Double-firing events, inconsistent UTMs, a consent banner quietly eating traffic. A model built on top inherits all of it, and plenty of my “we have a data problem” conversations land right here. I wrote about the flavours in[you don’t have a data problem](https://www.021newsletter.com/p/you-dont-have-a-data-problem).

None of these is attribution. All three are prerequisites, and each pays off on its own.

I don’t have a formula. When a lead comes in I do the sums in my head: what are they spending, what on, and can I find enough allocation decisions in that mix to beat my own fee. Above roughly $3M a year in paid media I’m confident I can. Below that it depends entirely on the mix, and the answer can be “no”.

So no number, just an order:

1.   **Prove a channel works** with a test, not a model.

2.   **Clean up the tracking** you already have.

3.   **Agree one ROAS definition** and get everyone calculating it the same way.

4.   **Model conversion value** if your conversions aren’t all worth the same.

5.   **Then** ask whether you need a model to split budget between channels.

Go after step five first and you’ll probably spend months confirming what the line already showed you.

If you’ve got a channel that works, a mix that’s genuinely hard to measure, and a funded plan to scale, that’s when this stops being premature. That’s the work we do at [Propel](https://partnerwithpropel.com/). If you’re not there yet, I’d rather say so.

Title: Paid Is Now the Only Guaranteed Slot in an AI Answer

URL Source: https://www.thestateofbrand.com/news/chatgpt-ads-paid-ai-answers

Published Time: 2026-09-08T20:56:53.310Z

Markdown Content:
Ask ChatGPT which CRM to buy and you'll get a sensible answer naming three or four vendors. On a free account, there's a good chance you'll also get a sponsored card underneath it for a fifth.

Seer Interactive flagged this in [its early read on ChatGPT ads](https://www.seerinteractive.com/insights/chatgpt-ads-insights), and it's the change that matters most for anyone who spent the last two years building toward AI citations. Search never quite produced this arrangement. A blue link and a text ad were different objects in different parts of the page, and users had twenty years of training in telling them apart. In a conversational answer they're inches from each other, in the same frame, and the sponsored one is the only one anybody can buy.

That's the trade the whole answer engine optimization category now has to explain. You can't purchase the recommendation. You can purchase the space beside it. Since the end of August, so can advertisers in about forty more countries.

## The number, and what OpenAI wants it to mean

On August 31 OpenAI said ChatGPT Ads had reached a $1 billion annualized revenue run rate, roughly 200 days after launch. [Axios](https://www.axios.com/2026/08/31/openai-chatgpt-ads-1b-revenue-run-rate), [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/08/31/open-ai-chatgpt-ads-revenue.html) and [SiliconANGLE](https://siliconangle.com/2026/08/31/openai-says-its-ad-business-has-already-hit-1b-in-annualized-revenue/) all ran it the same day. Alongside the announcement, OpenAI opened its self-serve Ads Manager to buyers in India, Europe, the Middle East and North Africa, having run it in the US since May.

Two bits of context change how that number reads. OpenAI pitched the milestone as evidence of a diversified business, and it did so under pressure to justify an $852 billion valuation ahead of an IPO. And per [Quartz](https://qz.com/openai-chatgpt-advertising-revenue-billion-083126), the company booked $6.7 billion in the second quarter alone. A billion a year, annualized, is a rounding error against that.

So the milestone isn't really a milestone. It's a proof of concept expensive enough to justify building more inventory.

The dissenting read is useful too. eMarketer's Nate Elliott told [Reuters](https://lufkindailynews.com/news_reuters/business/openais-ad-business-hits-1-billion-annualized-revenue-run-rate/article_56dba86d-7f95-50ec-88f8-a0bb1def417b.html) the announcement was "incredibly impressive and terribly disappointing," since a $1 billion run rate leaves OpenAI well short of a $2.5 billion advertising target for the year. Fast growth and a missed number at the same time. Companies behind plan on ad revenue don't respond by showing fewer ads.

## How fast this actually moved

Most marketing teams haven't tracked the rollout closely, and it's been quicker and messier than the coverage suggests.

OpenAI announced the test in January and switched it on for US free-tier users in February. Canada, Australia and New Zealand came in April. The self-serve Ads Manager opened to US businesses in May with CPC bidding. The UK went live in June, Japan not long after. By July the platform had picked up [conversion-based bidding, bulk campaign tools and mobile measurement integrations](https://www.techwyse.com/news/platform-updates/chatgpt-ads-ocpc-bidding-geo-exclusions-bulk-api-2026) with AppsFlyer and Adjust. Pricing started at a $60 CPM with a six-figure minimum and has since moved to open auction.

Eight months from closed pilot to self-serve buying in forty-plus markets. For comparison, Google took about two years to get ads into AI Overviews at similar breadth.

Only free and Go users see ads. [Plus, Pro, Business, Enterprise and Edu accounts remain ad-free](https://llmrefs.com/blog/chatgpt-ads), which means the ad layer is currently pointed at consumers and small businesses rather than the enterprise buyers most B2B brands are chasing. Early advertisers skewed accordingly, with HubSpot, Fiverr and [Top10.com](http://top10.com/) among the heaviest spenders in the spring. The format has stayed the same throughout: one labeled sponsored card per response, rendered with the answer. OpenAI's line is that ads are clearly marked, kept separate from how the model generates its answer, and that buyers can't see what users talk about.

## Be careful with the penetration numbers

You'll see a figure quoted a lot right now: ads in 51% of US replies. It comes from [Cloro's tracking panel](https://cloro.dev/blog/chatgpt-ads-penetration-study/) for the week ending July 3. A [later study from LLM Pulse](https://llmpulse.ai/blog/chatgpt-ads-study/), built on 137,038 answers across 70,760 distinct questions collected between late July and early August, put the US number at 72%.

Both are scraper panels. OpenAI publishes nothing, and the trend these trackers have captured is erratic enough that any single snapshot is close to meaningless. Penetration sat near zero through early spring, [jumped hard in late May](https://writesonic.com/blog/chatgpt-ads-rollout-study-may-2026), fell to 0.05% by mid-June, then climbed back past the earlier peak within a fortnight. Nobody outside OpenAI has explained the June pause, and nobody has ruled out another one.

The swings tell you more than the levels do. This isn't an ad product settling into a stable fill rate. It reads like a company finding out, in production, how much of its answer surface it can sell before users start complaining. Build a 2027 plan around 51% and you'll be wrong in one direction or the other. Build it around the direction of travel and you probably won't be.

## Google is doing the same thing, with more formats

Scoping this as an OpenAI story misses the larger half of it.

At Google Marketing Live in May the company introduced ad formats built specifically for AI Mode, including conversational discovery ads and a placement called Highlighted Answers. Serving in AI Mode and AI Overviews runs through Performance Max, AI Max, Shopping and broad match, which quietly turns eligibility into a question of campaign architecture rather than a separate media buy. Google has [confirmed](https://blog.google/products/ads-commerce/dsa-upgrade-to-ai-max-2026/) that Dynamic Search Ads, automatically created assets and campaign-level broad match all migrate onto AI Max starting this month.

Google has also been [testing ads in AI Mode against healthcare queries](https://browsermedia.agency/blog/ads-in-ai-mode-and-gml-2026-highlights/), limited to US advertisers on English-language searches. Regulated categories normally go last in any ad rollout. Starting there suggests the remaining question is scheduling, not whether.

## What this does to the case for AEO

The pitch for answer engine optimization always rested on an unstated assumption, which was that the AI answer is an unbought surface and that earning a place inside it buys you something durable. Budgets moved on that. So did a couple of hundred million dollars of venture funding into visibility tooling.

That assumption is now half wrong. Roughly half of US ChatGPT replies carry a commercial placement on the most conservative panel available, and whatever attention that placement takes comes off the same screen your earned mention is sitting on.

The awkward part is the asymmetry. An ad next to a category query is something you can buy on a Tuesday and see running by Wednesday. A citation is neither purchasable nor stable, and the trackers that watch it report heavy month-to-month turnover in which domains get cited. CFOs work that comparison out quickly, and they don't usually land on the side of the thing you can't buy or guarantee.

Meanwhile both platforms have committed themselves financially to expanding the paid layer. OpenAI needs the line to grow before an IPO. Google is moving its entire search ads stack onto AI surfaces on a published schedule. Neither has any reason to leave the answer box looking the way it did last year.

That doesn't make the AEO work worthless. Being named inside the recommendation is still a different and better thing than being an ad beside it, and no amount of spend gets you there. But you're running two programs on one screen now, and only one of them answers to you.

## Four things to do before Q4

Run your top twenty commercial prompts on a free ChatGPT account and write down which sponsored card appears with each. If a competitor is buying adjacency to answers that recommend you, that's a commercial problem this quarter, not a research project for next year.

Settle your position on defensive brand buying inside AI answers before someone forces it. The industry hasn't decided whether it's table stakes or an extortion tax. It had the identical argument about branded paid search around 2010 and came down on the side of buying.

Split earned and paid AI presence in your reporting. If they arrive on the same slide, nobody in the room will be able to say which one is working. Google's generative AI performance reports in Search Console [went out to every site worldwide on August 31](https://developers.google.com/search/blog/2026/06/gen-ai-performance-reports) and give you a free impressions baseline for AI Overviews, AI Mode and Discover, though [no click data yet](https://www.searchenginejournal.com/google-search-console-ai-reports-rolled-out-worldwide/587836/). There's no equivalent for ChatGPT and there probably won't be.

And stop briefing the answer box as a channel you can win outright. It's acquiring an organic layer and a paid layer, on the same trajectory as every surface before it, and the planning assumptions should match.

Title: Start here: Practical AI workflows for founders and GTM teams

URL Source: https://startupgtm.substack.com/p/start-here-practical-ai-workflows

Published Time: 2026-09-09T12:24:07+00:00

Markdown Content:
**If you’re using AI for sales, marketing, or running your business, you’ve probably collected plenty of prompts.**

The harder part is turning those prompts into work you can use.

*   What context should you provide?

*   What should the output contain?

*   What do you need to check before acting on it?

That’s what I write about in StartupGTM. I break down practical AI workflows with the prompts, examples, and implementation steps to try them in your own business.

[![Image 1](https://substackcdn.com/image/fetch/$s_!ALwf!,w_1456,c_limit,f_auto,q_auto:good,fl_progressive:steep/https%3A%2F%2Fsubstack-post-media.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fpublic%2Fimages%2F3ee3ca23-a69f-4963-9fa3-4b457318df1c_1448x1086.png)](https://substackcdn.com/image/fetch/$s_!ALwf!,f_auto,q_auto:good,fl_progressive:steep/https%3A%2F%2Fsubstack-post-media.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fpublic%2Fimages%2F3ee3ca23-a69f-4963-9fa3-4b457318df1c_1448x1086.png)

**Here are four places to start.**

Company size, industry, and job title help you build a list.

> **They don’t explain why someone would care about your offer right now.**

The Pressure Profile ICP System adds organizational pressure, role-specific tension, behavioral triggers, and emotional context.

It includes prompts for developing a profile and questions for checking whether the output reflects your buyers’ actual situation.

[![Image 2](https://substackcdn.com/image/fetch/$s_!6tWz!,w_1456,c_limit,f_auto,q_auto:good,fl_progressive:steep/https%3A%2F%2Fsubstack-post-media.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fpublic%2Fimages%2F208fe52e-8d08-45b4-8237-5107e10a59a7_1024x1024.png)](https://substackcdn.com/image/fetch/$s_!6tWz!,f_auto,q_auto:good,fl_progressive:steep/https%3A%2F%2Fsubstack-post-media.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fpublic%2Fimages%2F208fe52e-8d08-45b4-8237-5107e10a59a7_1024x1024.png)

**[Read: The Pressure Profile ICP System →](https://startupgtm.substack.com/p/the-pressure-profile-icp-system)**

Your business model, constraints, and current priorities shouldn’t need a fresh explanation every time you open a chat.

**The Context Stack organizes that information into three layers: who you are, what you’re working on, and how you want AI to work with you.**

The edition includes builder prompts for creating your context files.

[![Image 3](https://substackcdn.com/image/fetch/$s_!2O0d!,w_1456,c_limit,f_auto,q_auto:good,fl_progressive:steep/https%3A%2F%2Fsubstack-post-media.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fpublic%2Fimages%2F7bf3f797-7738-4b6c-81d5-9fabafd7db82_770x756.jpeg)](https://substackcdn.com/image/fetch/$s_!2O0d!,f_auto,q_auto:good,fl_progressive:steep/https%3A%2F%2Fsubstack-post-media.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fpublic%2Fimages%2F7bf3f797-7738-4b6c-81d5-9fabafd7db82_770x756.jpeg)

**[Read: The Context Stack →](https://startupgtm.substack.com/p/the-context-stack)**

> **A content audit should help you decide what to change, not just report which posts got likes.**

The Content Trust Analysis System examines recognition, credibility, risk reduction, and commitment.

Use its diagnostic prompts to identify where your content needs stronger evidence, better objection handling, or a clearer next step.

[![Image 4](https://substackcdn.com/image/fetch/$s_!0h2V!,w_1456,c_limit,f_auto,q_auto:good,fl_progressive:steep/https%3A%2F%2Fsubstack-post-media.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fpublic%2Fimages%2Fe8d21796-c04d-4317-ae1a-c2eaadb7b403_865x799.jpeg)](https://substackcdn.com/image/fetch/$s_!0h2V!,f_auto,q_auto:good,fl_progressive:steep/https%3A%2F%2Fsubstack-post-media.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fpublic%2Fimages%2Fe8d21796-c04d-4317-ae1a-c2eaadb7b403_865x799.jpeg)

**[Read: The Content Trust Analysis System →](https://startupgtm.substack.com/p/content-trust-analysis-system)**

Sorting sales replies, researching multiple accounts, and reviewing drafts need different workflows.

**Dynamic Workflows for GTM explains six patterns for organizing this work,** including splitting repeated tasks, routing different inputs, and separating creation from critique.

[![Image 5: what is dynamic workflow](https://substackcdn.com/image/fetch/$s_!DITm!,w_1456,c_limit,f_auto,q_auto:good,fl_progressive:steep/https%3A%2F%2Fsubstack-post-media.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fpublic%2Fimages%2F6558bca1-464e-4f32-a747-89293ed57219_1672x941.png)](https://substackcdn.com/image/fetch/$s_!DITm!,f_auto,q_auto:good,fl_progressive:steep/https%3A%2F%2Fsubstack-post-media.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fpublic%2Fimages%2F6558bca1-464e-4f32-a747-89293ed57219_1672x941.png)

**[Read: Dynamic Workflows for GTM →](https://startupgtm.substack.com/p/dynamic-workflows-for-gtm-six-patterns)**

Your competitor research, customer insights, and market notes become more useful when you can find them, connect them, and check where an answer came from.

**The GTM Knowledge System Kit gives you schemas, prompts, templates, and setup guides** for organizing that material into a knowledge base you can query with AI.

> Your welcome email will include the access link, and you’ll receive future editions with more practical AI workflows.

**Already subscribed?**

**[Get the kit here →](https://poddarayush.gumroad.com/l/gtm-ai-knowledge-builder-kit)**

Choose DIY Kit, enter $0, and complete checkout to download it.

Start with QUICKSTART.md and one source document.

Follow the first-ingest instructions, ask a question, and check the output against your original source before adding more.

_AI can miss details or invent them; review is part of the workflow._

Ayush
